scholarships.title: Pacific Regional Sports Research Scholarship (PRSRS)
scholarships.official_source: Oceania National Olympic Committee and The University of the South Pacific

eligibility: Be a citizen of a USP member country (Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Niue, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tokelau, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu)
Preferably be 40 years or younger at the time of application
Apply for a Master's by research degree at USP
Propose a project within economics, social impact or physical education with a focus on sports
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of a USP member country, preferably 40 or younger, applying for a Master's by research degree at USP on a sports-focused project.
benefits: Book allowance of up to FJD 750 per year
Living allowance of FJD 21,600 per year
Dependants Allowance of FJD 10,883.00 per year for qualifying awardees
Establishment Allowance of FJD 1,942.00 one-off for qualifying awardees
Research grant only after the research plan and budget are approved by the relevant Academic Unit Research Committee
One return airfare when the award holder must travel to a USP campus in another country

requirements: Not permitted to be in paid employment during the tenure of the award
Contribute a maximum of eight hours per week to ongoing teaching for one semester
Complete an industry placement for another semester, on terms agreed on confirmation of award
application_method: Submit an application as USP directs for the PRSRS call on the postgraduate scholarships page
Contact the USP Research Student Coordinator for the current application instructions
existing.selection_notes: The scholarship is a collaboration between the Oceania National Olympic Committee and USP, and both partners fund interdisciplinary projects within economics, social impact and physical education with a focus on sports. Three scholarships were awarded for the 2026 academic year.
existing.best_fit: Pacific students from any USP member country, 40 or younger, seeking a Master's by research at USP on the economics, social impact or physical education of sport.
existing.notes: All amounts on the official page are in Fijian dollars. Awards may be held in any USP member country.
existing.duration: One year of full-time Master's by research study plus a semester of teaching contribution and a semester of industry placement, terms agreed on confirmation of award
existing.application_period: The official page is marked CLOSED; awards for the 2026 academic year are tenable from early 2026 and three scholarships were available. USP publishes a new call annually on the same page.
existing.program_type: Joint research scholarship (Oceania National Olympic Committee with the University of the South Pacific)
